description: JavaScript algorithm practice using Judge0. Draft assessment pending expert review and pilot calibration; covers only the stated tasks, not all JavaScript proficiency.

questions.title: Two Sum Target Matcher
questions.prompt: Implement solution(numsStr, target) in JavaScript. numsStr is a comma-separated string of integers. Return two different zero-based indices as a string 'i,j' whose values sum to target. Scan the second index j from left to right and return the first matching pair; for repeated values, use the most recent earlier index. Return an empty string if no pair exists. Example: solution('2,7,11,15', 9) returns '0,1'. Test inputs use JSON argument arrays, for example ["2,7,11,15",9].
questions.solutionCode: function solution(numsStr, target) { const nums = String(numsStr).split(',').map(Number); const seen = new Map(); for (let j = 0; j < nums.length; j++) { const other = Number(target) - nums[j]; if (seen.has(other)) return seen.get(other) + ',' + j; seen.set(nums[j], j); } return ''; }

criteria: Find distinct indices with the specified tie-break

questions.title: Valid Palindrome Verifier
questions.prompt: Implement solution(str) in JavaScript. Keep only ASCII letters A-Z/a-z and digits 0-9, ignore letter case, and return boolean true if the remaining string reads identically forward and backward; otherwise return false. An empty normalized string is a palindrome. Example: solution('A man, a plan, a canal: Panama') returns true. Test inputs use JSON argument arrays, preserving commas and whitespace inside strings.
questions.solutionCode: function solution(str) { const clean = String(str).toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, ''); return clean === clean.split('').reverse().join(''); }

criteria: Preserve single string input including punctuation

testCases.input: ["A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"]
["Was it a car or a cat I saw?"]
